_readme: Identifiers this registry publishes that no CASA specification defines. Each is a namespace FAR had to choose in order to name assets that exist, and each is therefore a concrete proposal the ChainAgnostic Standards Alliance would need to ratify for these identifiers to be interoperable rather than ours alone. Published so the gap is visible and actionable rather than hidden behind a confidence label.

_upstreamNote: CASA's CONTRIBUTING expects a namespace to be proposed by people who can speak for that ecosystem — the editors ask for interlocutors and reviewers familiar with it, and the merged PRs are authored by ecosystem insiders. FAR is a consumer of these identifiers, not a representative of those chains, so an unsolicited PR from us is likely to stall for want of ecosystem sign-off. Where a proposal already exists we align with it rather than duplicating it; where none exists, the honest contribution is to raise the gap with the ecosystem rather than to speak for it.

chainsIdentifiedWithNoNamespace._readme: Chains that ISO 24165 (DTIF) already assigns a ledger identifier to, which we positively identified — in most cases from the anchor block hash DTIF itself publishes — and for which ChainAgnostic/namespaces has NO namespace at all. These are not ambiguous chains: the anchor hash is a verifiable genesis. They are the sharpest evidence that the CAIP identifier space lags what a formal standards body already registers.

Internet Computer.note: ICP's subnet/canister architecture has no single chain-level identifier that any ratified namespace expresses.

VITE.note: Vite uses a block-lattice/DAG with a snapshot chain; there is no CAIP-2 shape defined for it.

Ardor.note: Ardor's parent chain plus child chains (Ignis etc.) would additionally need a sub-chain convention that no CAIP defines.

BitShares.note: BitShares, Steem and Hive are all Graphene chains in this batch and all fail for the same reason - only Hive got a ratified namespace.

NEM.note: Distinct ledger from Symbol (also in this batch), which likewise has no namespace.

v.systems.note: v.systems is a Scorex/Waves-lineage SPoS chain; the ratified 'waves' namespace covers Waves itself, not this derivative.

Aeternity.note: Chain identification is solid; only the namespace is missing.

Nebulas.note: The only 'Nebulas' match in the EVM registry is 'Unicorn Ultra Nebulas Testnet' (eip155:2484), an unrelated project.

Siacoin.note: Sia is a UTXO-like chain but uses BLAKE2b, not double-SHA-256, so bip122 (which is defined over Bitcoin-family genesis hashes) is not a defensible fit.

Atto.note: Same structural problem as Nano in this batch: block-lattice ledgers have no CAIP-2 shape defined.

NKN.note: An ERC-20 NKN also exists on Ethereum, but that is a different ledger from the native chain this DLI names.

Nuls.note: Do not substitute eip155:119 - ENULS is a distinct ledger from the NULS main chain named here.

Kaspa.note: Do not substitute eip155:104566 - KaspaClassic is a different chain from Kaspa.

Nano.note: Nano does have a well-known genesis open block hash, so a future 'nano' namespace could use it - but nothing ratified consumes it today.
